tier_rules.v1_profile_catalog: Profiles that belong to the v1 stable catalog. This is not a bundle requirement; implementations MUST claim only the profiles, event kinds, schemas, and operations they actually support.
tier_rules.v1_minimal_interop_floor: Minimum profile for claiming v1 Event Store interop. Higher-level client, service, federation, blob, push, identity, and sovereign profiles remain independently claimable.
tier_rules.extension_profile_implementation: Optional. Tracks evolving external standards (MIMI Internet-Drafts; A2A/ACP/MCP unstandardized agent protocols; Applet registry/audit SLA). Implementations claiming v1 core MAY omit these entirely. When the underlying external standards mature, replacement profiles with stable version pinning will supersede these entries.

candidate_profiles_tier_rule: Profiles pairing unregistered candidate workflow concept/action names / capabilities with an explicit fail-closed gate. Receivers MUST treat any capability action whose `profile` points to a candidate profile as unknown (risk_tier=high default) unless they implement the profile. Candidate profiles are NOT part of v1 active conformance and SHOULD be promoted (with paired wire Event.kind values registered under `cx.*`) once their underlying surface is formally registered.
profile_roles_rule: Every profile id MUST be annotated with exactly one role from the enum {client, server, gateway, directory, admin, interop}. Roles partition the profile namespace so that an implementation MUST NOT mistake e.g. a gateway profile (push_gateway, blob_node) for a client profile, or a deployment / hardening / vector profile (admin role) for a wire-conformance client / server profile. SDK manifests, client-side feature negotiation, and conformance harness loaders MUST consult `profile_roles` before claiming a profile as locally implemented. Roles in spec layer metadata; the per-profile object in `profile_requirements` MAY ALSO carry a `role` field for convenience, but `profile_roles` is the canonical source.

cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.summary: Degraded E2EE profile. Allows `mls_send_pause="advisory"` (cf. §2.4.1) so that low-latency interactive scenarios (real-time AV, collaborative editing, in-game chat) do not block message send on MLS commit completion. Cost: removed members can continue decrypting a small window of subsequent messages. NOT for general chat / collaboration / compliance use. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with cx.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers that do not advertise cx.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 MUST reject Realm create / cx.realm.policy_components writes that set mls_send_pause="advisory" (reason: profile_unsupported / mls_send_pause_advisory_requires_e2ee_relaxed_profile). They MUST NOT silently accept the advisory string without honoring the relaxed semantics.

client_ui_requirements.banner_warning: Realms declaring this profile MUST display a banner-level warning indicating that kick / ban is not cryptographically immediate; the warning MAY be temporarily collapsed but MUST NOT be permanently dismissable.
client_ui_requirements.invite_warning: When a user invites a new member, the UI SHOULD prompt with 'this Realm uses degraded E2EE' so the invitee can make an informed decision.
client_ui_requirements.export_marker: Sync metadata / backup / export MUST preserve a `e2ee_relaxed=true` marker so downstream consumers know the cryptographic guarantee is relaxed.

downgrade_window_constraint.rationale: Receiving client refuses to admit a message into verified timeline if the gap between receive_at and the most recent membership_change_at exceeds this window with old-epoch decryption.
downgrade_window_constraint.receiver_enforcement: Receiver MUST enforce the hard ceiling independently of any declared deployment value: if a Realm policy event sets relaxed_window_max_ms > absolute_hard_ceiling_ms (300000 ms / 5 min), the reducer MUST reject the policy update with reason_code `relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling` (mapped from `schema_violation`), and the receiver MUST treat the policy event as failed_precondition. Receivers MUST NOT silently clamp the value to the ceiling, because a silent clamp would let a deployment publish a longer window than receivers honor and split visible policy state across implementations. Negative vector: `cx.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1` covers (a) reducer reject on policy write > 300000 ms, (b) receiver reject on old-epoch decrypt admission when the gap exceeds the per-policy declared window, and (c) reject when any deployment tries to redefine the ceiling via an unrelated profile.
downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled: Profiles in the compliance / audited tier (cx.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1, cx.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1, and any deployment declaring `audit_assurance >= disclosed_policy`) MUST NOT enable cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Reducer MUST reject the combination with reason_code `e2ee_relaxed_disallowed_in_compliance_profile`. Rationale: compliance assurance presumes the kick-out semantic is cryptographically immediate; the relaxed window contradicts that presumption.

cx.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.compliance_unfit: Compliance / regulatory contexts that require 'kick-out is immediately effective' MUST NOT use this profile. Use non-E2EE Realm (encryption_profile="none") + enclave channels instead. Spec deliberately does not allow further relaxation than this profile; deployments needing more leniency are out of v1 E2EE scope.

cx.profile.directory_service.v1.description: Contrix v1 Directory Service profile. Directory Services index resource-signed discovery state, expose blinded search/resolve endpoints, and support at least one §8 ingest mode without becoming a source of truth.

cx.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1.description: High-assurance / sovereign / regulated / multi-writer federation profile. Adds mandatory proactive frontier exchange with fail-state semantics on top of the cx.profile.federation_minimal.v1 baseline. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.3 and zh/sync/sovereign-deployment.md §11.1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: reject claim of cx.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1 if proactive frontier exchange or stale_peer fail-state is not implemented

additional_requirements.frontier_probe_capability_must: Peer MUST expose capability-gated frontier probe endpoint per federation.md §4.5.1.
additional_requirements.proactive_exchange_must: Per federation-visible Realm, per authorized peer, frontier probe interval MUST be <= 3600 seconds.
additional_requirements.fail_state_must: Three consecutive probe failures (peer unreachable, signature failure, frontier_root divergence beyond fork-resolution threshold) MUST mark the peer as 'stale_peer' for that Realm.
additional_requirements.stale_peer_behavior_must: While a peer is in 'stale_peer' state: MUST quarantine its push payloads (no local frontier advancement); MUST surface state via operator alarm channel; MAY refuse to fanout new Events to that peer. Stale status MUST clear after successful fork resolution (head reconvergence or quorum witness attestation alignment).

cx.profile.push_gateway.v1.description: Push gateway base profile. Provides the device registration / notify operation surface. All implementations claiming this profile MUST also implement cx.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (default interop privacy baseline) — see zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §5.1. Visible-payload variants are opt-in only via cx.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1.

cx.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1.description: Default push gateway privacy baseline. Every implementation claiming cx.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile. Provider-facing payloads MUST NOT carry stable identifying fields (principal DID, sender DID, Realm id / name / avatar, Flow id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction value, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key). Payloads MUST be restricted to per-(recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) pairwise pseudonym push_target_id + closed-enum wakeup hint fields (wakeup_kind, badge_count, unread_increment, l10n_key). See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §4.5 / §5.1 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5a.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: MUST fail closed; gateways unable to enforce blind wakeup MUST NOT claim cx.profile.push_gateway.v1

additional_requirements.stable_identifier_ban_must: Provider payload MUST NOT contain principal DID, sender DID / handle, Realm id / name, Flow id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction emoji, attachment filename, IP, geolocation, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key.
additional_requirements.pseudonym_scope_must: push_target_id MUST be a pairwise pseudonym scoped to (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route); MUST NOT be reusable across Principal Server contexts.
additional_requirements.default_claim_must: Any implementation claiming cx.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile and MUST NOT advertise downgrade switches that disable blind wakeup.

cx.profile.push_gateway.visible_notifica.description: Opt-in push gateway profile for deployments that require visible notification fields (e.g. titles, sender labels) in provider payloads. Claiming this profile is permitted ONLY when (1) Realm policy explicitly lists the gateway in plaintext_visible_services AND declares visible_notification allowance, (2) per-device opt-in is recorded in cx.device authorization state, and (3) the client UI clearly surfaces that visible-notification mode is active. Even when claimed, payloads MUST stay minimised: no message body, no DID URL, no cross-Realm stable correlation key, no IP / geolocation, no free-form text outside the profile-declared field set. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; deployments that cannot guarantee Realm policy + device opt-in + UI disclosure MUST NOT claim this profile

additional_requirements.policy_gate_must: Realm policy MUST list the gateway service DID in plaintext_visible_services with visible_notification explicitly allowed.
additional_requirements.device_opt_in_must: Each receiving device MUST record an opt-in flag in its authorization state; absent opt-in, sender / Realm service MUST fall back to blind wakeup.
additional_requirements.ui_disclosure_must: Client UI MUST clearly indicate visible notification is active to the user.
additional_requirements.payload_minimisation_must: Even when claimed, payload MUST NOT carry message body, DID URLs, cross-Realm stable correlation keys, IP / geolocation, or untyped free-form text.

cx.profile.push_gateway.matrix_passthrou.description: Interop compatibility profile for Matrix push gateway passthrough. Implementations claiming this profile MAY accept Matrix-shaped push gateway payloads as a bridge for legacy clients but MUST NOT mix this profile with cx.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 on the same notify path: the Matrix push gateway shape carries identifying fields incompatible with the default Contrix privacy baseline. Bridges MUST partition traffic so that any peer or device negotiated under cx.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (i.e. the default v1 baseline) NEVER receives a matrix_passthrough payload. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1 and zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §11.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; bridges that cannot partition traffic MUST NOT claim this profile

additional_requirements.partition_must: Bridges MUST partition push traffic so that Contrix v1 default-baseline peers (cx.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1) NEVER receive matrix_passthrough-shaped payloads.
additional_requirements.no_default_mixing_must: Implementations MUST NOT advertise both cx.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 and cx.profile.push_gateway.matrix_passthrough.v1 as applying to the same (recipient_service_did, device) tuple.
additional_requirements.interop_only_must: This profile is interop-only; it MUST NOT be used as a substitute for cx.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 in default Contrix deployments.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: require explicit grant before join or tool use

Servers not declaring this profile MUST reject cx.agent_task.* and cx.content.import_attestation writes targeting a Realm declaring cx.profile.agent_workspace.v1 (profile_unsupported). Source-Realm mention_redirect acceptance is governed independently by the cx.feature.mention_redirect.v1 critical_extension check.

cx.profile.agent_workspace.governed.v1.summary: Governed-source profile. Declared by a SOURCE Realm that wishes its export policy enforced at the mirror-side reducer (not just at source-side agent runtime). Mirror reducer MUST reject cx.content.import_attestation events lacking a valid source-side cx.schema.content.source_export_policy_attestation.v1 envelope, instead of accepting + audit-marking as permissive cx.profile.agent_workspace.v1 does.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers that do not implement governed_import MUST fail-closed (profile_unsupported) when asked to accept a cx.content.import_attestation whose claimed source Realm declares cx.profile.agent_workspace.governed.v1; they MUST NOT silently downgrade to permissive accept-then-audit. See agent-workspace-profile.md §8.2 governed behavior + §9.1.

policy_authority_declaration.description: Source Realm declares which DIDs are authorized to sign source_export_policy_attestation envelopes. Attestation `authority_did` MUST appear in this list.

ttl_constraints.rationale: Mirror reducers SHOULD cache attestations only as long as the source-issued TTL allows; longer-lived attestations let revoked export decisions stay accepted.

cx.profile.agent_workspace.strict.v1.summary: Reserved placeholder for a hardening variant of agent_workspace addressing stale-window concerns in cross-deployment / third-party-runtime / multi-tenant SaaS / regulatory-immediate-revocation scenarios. Candidate mechanisms (any or combination): frontier freshness gate (sync-verify source frontier covers latest revoke before each agent action), source-issued lease (short-TTL pass-through, fail-closed on expiry), protocol-level hard stale window upper bound. The id is registered as `status: reserved` so prose can reference it as a direction without breaking lint, and so downstream registries / SDKs see the name as known-reserved rather than typo / drift.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Reserved id with no conformance requirements bound yet. Deployments needing stricter freshness MAY define their own private profile in the interim and graduate to this id once it is filled with normative requirements.

cx.profile.agent_workspace.strict.v1.notes: See agent-workspace-profile.md §1.1 for the trust-model boundary that distinguishes the default scope from the scenarios this reserved profile would address.

cx.profile.agent_workspace.lite.v1.summary: Lightweight profile for single-controller mirror Realm that does NOT need the full audit-grade lattice. Strips: (a) anchor-based reservation TTL (reverts to wall-clock + grace), (b) per-task transparency / source_authority FSM cells (controller checks state via UI hint, not lattice), (c) MLS Governance Binding requirement. Keeps: reservation cell namespaces (mirror_space_by_source / mirror_flow_by_source), import_attestation envelope, mention_redirect content block. Cross-Realm writes (publish-back to source Realm) MUST still go through full pipeline regardless of lite profile.

ttl_clock_source.rationale: Lite deployments tolerate replay-attack-against-cleanup as long as controller is the only authority writing tasks; coarse wall-clock TTL is acceptable.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers declaring lite MUST also accept all base agent_workspace.v1 read paths (lite is a strict subset of writes, not reads). Source-Realm side handling of mention_redirect is unchanged.

cross_space_writes_unchanged.rule: Lite ONLY relaxes mirror-internal lattice. Any event leaving the mirror Realm and entering a source / shared Realm MUST go through the standard pipeline (signature, capability, schema, full lattice, MLS group of the destination Realm). Lite is not a justification for cross-Realm shortcuts.

cx.profile.agent_workspace.lite.v1.notes: Lite is intended for hobbyist / single-developer setups where the controller is also the only auditor. Deployments that publish or share mirror state with anyone except the workspace owner SHOULD NOT use lite. See agent-workspace-profile.md §9.2 for prose normative.

cx.profile.franking.sender_commitment.v1.description: Opt-in sender-bound plaintext commitment for E2EE Realms. Adds a sidecar (unsigned.franking.sender_commitment) carrying an HMAC-SHA-256 tag derived from per-device-per-epoch MLS exporter secret over plaintext+aad+ciphertext+epoch_local_seq, enabling audit verifiers to independently attribute plaintext to (sender_device_id, epoch). Does NOT change core franking wire shape (sidecar lives in unsigned scope). Does NOT provide outside-of-group non-repudiation — verifier attribution is bounded by MLS epoch deniability and verifier's exporter-secret retention window (default <= 72h). Plaintext sender attribution from reporter evidence MUST go through §3.4.2 verification flow. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4.2.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: deployments not implementing this profile MUST NOT emit unsigned.franking.sender_commitment and MUST treat received sender_commitment as unknown extension

additional_requirements.key_derivation_must: Sender Commitment Key MUST be HKDF-Expand-Label over the MLS epoch exporter_secret with label='cx franking sender commitment v1' and context binding {mls_group_id, epoch, sender_device_id}.
additional_requirements.commitment_tag_must: HMAC-SHA-256 over canonical bytes binding plaintext_digest, aad_digest, sender_device_id, mls_group_id, epoch, epoch_local_seq, ciphertext_digest; truncated to 128-bit tag.
additional_requirements.epoch_local_seq_must: Unique per (sender_device_id, epoch); reducer/verifier MUST persist a seen-set or equivalent exact replay filter and reject duplicate seq values (reason sender_commitment_seq_replay). Out-of-order report submission MUST NOT be rejected solely because seq is lower than a later observed value.
additional_requirements.verifier_window_must: Implementations MUST document their verifier exporter-secret retention window; commitments outside that window are unverifiable, NOT forged.
additional_requirements.plaintext_brute_force_must: Deployments MUST NOT combine this profile with governance models where verifiers can offline-brute-force candidate plaintexts against the commitment without prior gating.

cx.profile.morph.schema_migration_transf.description: Opt-in Realm profile that permits cx.morph.schema_migrate.v1 events with compatibility_class in {breaking, transformation}. Realms not declaring this profile MUST reject such migrations as morph_schema_refs_transformation_unsupported. Profile commits the deployment to deterministic, replay-safe per-field transformation_rules[] and to capability gating cx.morph.schema.migrate at an audit-grade tier. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: deployments without this profile MUST reject breaking and transformation migrations even if the event-payload schema would accept them

additional_requirements.capability_must: Reducer MUST require cx.morph.schema.migrate (or Realm-declared equivalent) capability at the event's frontier; missing yields capability_denied.
additional_requirements.from_set_check_must: Reducer MUST set-equal-compare payload.from_schema_refs[] against the Morph's current schema_refs[] at apply time; mismatch yields failed_precondition.
additional_requirements.deterministic_transformation_must: Any transformation_rules[] MUST be replay-deterministic across implementations; profile vectors MUST cover identity, rename, type widening, and default backfill cases.

identity.downgrade_note: Personal node MAY use did:web as principal method when explicitly declared. Upgrade to small_team or higher MUST migrate to did:webvh per identity-did.md §4.2.2.

cx.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v.description: MLS Governance Binding (full): the v1 hardening profile that binds MLS epochs to governance state. Required for E2EE Realms. MLS commits are Moves carrying a governance_binding payload (membership_frontier / policy_root / capability_root / discussion_metadata_hash, transcript-hashed via the cx_governance_binding GroupContext extension) and update three cells (mls_epoch, key_schedule, covered_frontier). E2EE message Moves must prove the covered_frontier cell contains the required governance Anchor frontier; governance / recovery Moves do not depend on it.

cx.profile.mls.minimal_metadata_space.v1.description: Hardening profile for E2EE Realms that route by room-scoped pairwise DID and keep principal DID, device identity, display profile, and relationship graph inside encrypted identity_link payloads.

cx.profile.matrix_compat.v1.description: Optional Matrix interop compatibility profile. Declares wire-shape parity for the directly Matrix-derived surfaces: /sync (since/next_batch + lazy_load_members), to-device queue, /keys/upload|query|claim, push gateway facade, cross-signing key hierarchy, SAS verification message flow. Implementations claiming this profile MUST treat the cx.* names of these surfaces as semantically equivalent to their Matrix counterparts so that Matrix client SDK code can be reused with only adapter changes. This profile does NOT add new wire fields; it is a conformance assertion about behavioural equivalence.

cx.profile.candidate.join_policy.v1.description: Candidate profile pairing the still-unregistered join-policy workflow concept/action names (`realm.join_policy`, `member.application`, `member.application.review`, `member.application.cancel`; see zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §4.1) with the gating capability action `cx.realm.join.review`. These bare names are not v1 wire Event.kind values. The action remains in the canonical capability registry so prose can reference it stably, but receivers that do not implement this profile MUST treat `cx.realm.join.review` as unknown (capability-action-registry.json registry_rules: 'Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default)'). Claiming the profile commits the implementation to the candidate join-policy workflow surface defined in zh/governance/join-policy.md. This profile is not part of v1 active conformance; it will be promoted with registered `cx.*` Event.kind values when join-policy is formally registered.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim (and reject member.application.* events as unknown)

cx.profile.key_backup.memory_hard.v1.description: Hardening profile for passphrase-protected key backups. Requires memory-hard Argon2id defaults, explicit PBKDF2 downgrade, domain-separated backup classes, and deterministic AEAD nonce recomputation.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim or reject weak passphrase_kdf backups

cx.profile.cross_signing.reset.v1.description: Hardening profile for high-risk cross-signing reset. Claimants MUST accept cx.cross_signing.reset only with one valid reset proof family, enforce generation monotonicity, clock skew, and replay rejection, and require a successor cx.cross_signing.publish within the recovery window. Verification rules and reason codes are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

max_clock_skew_seconds.rationale: Maximum allowed deviation between `cx.cross_signing.reset.issued_at` and receiver local clock. Default 300s mirrors policy-decision freshness windows; receivers MAY tighten down to 60s for high-assurance deployments or relax up to 900s for federated peers with documented clock skew. Beyond the configured value receivers MUST emit cross_signing_reset_clock_skew_exceeded.

publish_recovery_window_seconds.rationale: Maximum interval after an accepted reset within which the successor cx.cross_signing.publish MUST be observed; receivers MUST otherwise enter the 'no usable SSK/USK' state from §14.2 step 5. Default 24h matches the §14.1 normative requirement.

reset_replay_cache_min_retention_seconds.rationale: Minimum retention for the (principal_id, previous_generation) replay-rejection cache used by §14.4 通用规则. MUST be at least `publish_recovery_window_seconds + 3600` so that no late-arriving duplicate reset can bypass the cache before the successor publish window closes. Default = 24h + 1h slack.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: fail closed or omit profile claim
